critical_code_review_comments: _consume_free_grant rewritten in iter63 from insert+catch-DuplicateKey to atomic find_one_and_update($inc count, $setOnInsert first_used_at, upsert=True) with return_document=True. Verified race-safe under 8-way asyncio.gather: exactly 1 allowed, 7 denied, 1 doc, count converges to 8. Defence-in-depth recommendation from iter62 is now satisfied — no longer relies on the unique compound index alone.

PDF export at /api/solve/sessions/{sid}/export.pdf uses StreamingResponse with iter([pdf_bytes]). For very large PDFs this loads everything in memory before streaming — fine for current 4-10KB session output but flag for future if briefings PDFs grow. Content-Disposition uses 'inline' — correct for browser preview UX.

_draft_cycle_questions falls back gracefully to the deterministic _to_question() chain when LLM fails. JSON parsing only accepts dict with 'questions' key — if LLM returns a bare array the fallback kicks in. Acceptable, but a tiny bit defensive coding (accepting List[str] OR {questions: [...]}) would survive prompt drift.

GET /api/solve/pro-status correctly does NOT consume the grant — uses find_one (read-only), unlike _consume_free_grant. Good separation. is_pro reads plan from account doc — make sure billing webhook updates account.plan when subscription activates (out-of-scope for this test pass).

solve_engine.py is now 1046 lines (up from 931 in iter62) — the maintainability suggestion to split into solve_handoffs.py + solve_export.py still stands; not blocking but increasing tech debt with each iter.
